author: evergreen reporter
title: East Tennessee couple indicted on federal child exploitation charges
text:
A federal grand jury in Jackson, Tennessee has indicted Randall Scott Sharpe, 56, and Tina Angelique Sharpe, 61, both of Granville, Tennessee, on multiple charges related to federal child sexual exploitation. The indictment alleges that the couple used a minor in their custody to produce visual depictions of sexually explicit conduct during two separate periods in May and September 2024 in Bolivar, Tennessee.
The defendants are also accused of possessing images involving a minor under the age of 12 engaged in sexually explicit conduct during those same periods. Additionally, Randall Sharpe faces two counts of coercion and enticement of a minor for alleged electronic communications with the same minor in November 2024.
United States Attorney D. Michael Dunavant announced the return of the indictment. The case is being heard by United States District Court Judge S. Thomas Anderson in Jackson.
If convicted on the production charges, both defendants face mandatory minimum sentences of 15 years and up to 30 years in prison for each count. The possession charges carry a maximum sentence of 20 years each. For the enticement charges against Randall Sharpe, there is a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years and up to life imprisonment for each count. Federal law does not allow parole.
“This case is being investigated by agents with the FBI Nashville Division, Jackson and Memphis Resident Agencies, and officers with the Bolivar Police Department,” according to officials.
Authorities encourage anyone with information about this case or any other incidents involving abuse of minors to contact either the FBI Nashville Division at 615-232-7500 or the Bolivar Police Department at 731-658-4284.
Assistant United States Attorneys Josh Morrow and Christie Hopper are prosecuting this case for the government.
Officials emphasized: “The charges and allegations contained in the indictment are merely accusations of criminal conduct, not evidence. The defendants are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt and convicted through due process of law.”
